name: Blurt
one_liner: Hold a key, talk, and polished text lands wherever you are typing on your Mac.

text.why: Built-in Mac dictation behaves differently in every app and the result shows it. Blurt gives you one key anywhere, with no subscription and no account: it calls AssemblyAI with a key you own, and every line that sends the audio is readable.
text.take: The pipeline is simple enough to follow with your eyes, and it says on the first line that the audio goes to an external API rather than burying it.
build: Native AppKit and SwiftUI — no Electron, no web views. The whole pipeline is one dependency-free Swift package: capture the microphone, one request, paste at the caret. No local models, no background daemon, no job queue. The app is signed and notarised.

who.role: Mac users who would rather speak their mail and documents, and anyone cutting down on typing.

start.text: Get the app from assemblyai.com/blurt and paste in an AssemblyAI key of your own.

caveat: The audio goes to AssemblyAI. The app itself is free and MIT, but the API bills by usage and you must create the key yourself. macOS only.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: Blurt in use: spoken words arriving as clean sentences in the app that has focus.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
